title: Dimension shifting for Tor along a free presentation, natural in the second variable
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $0\to K\to F\to M\to0$ be a short exact sequence of $R$-modules [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence] with $F$ a free $R$-module [def-weil-pbc-free-module], and let $i\ge1$ be an integer. Then for every $R$-module $N$ there is an isomorphism of $R$-modules $\theta_N:\operatorname{Tor}^R_{i+1}(M,N)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Tor}^R_i(K,N)$, with $\operatorname{Tor}$ and its functoriality in the second variable as in [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules], and these isomorphisms are natural in $N$: for every $R$-linear map $g:N\to N'$ one has $\theta_{N'}\circ\operatorname{Tor}^R_{i+1}(M,g)=\operatorname{Tor}^R_i(K,g)\circ\theta_N$.

source.place: Algebra, Section Tag 00LY (section-tor) with Lemma Tag 00LZ (lemma-tor-welldefined, maps of resolutions induce the functoriality) and Lemma Tag 00M0 (lemma-long-exact-sequence-tor); the dimension shift is stated in the proof of Lemma Tag 00S2 ('Since $N^0$ is free, we also see that Tor_2^B(H^0,C)=Tor_1^B(M,C)'); naturality in N: the isomorphism is the connecting map of the long exact Tor sequence in the first variable, which commutes with maps in the second variable

proof.text: Fix Mathlib CategoryTheory.projectiveResolution of K = S.X₁, independently of N. The definition of Tor permits projective resolutions [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules], so no compatible free-resolution horseshoe construction is needed.

Splice this resolution Q to the given short exact sequence [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence]: P₀ = S.X₂, Pₙ₊₁ = Qₙ, d₁ = η followed by S.f, and augmentation S.g. Freeness [def-weil-pbc-free-module] makes P₀ projective; the remaining terms are projective. Exactness at P₀ follows by comparing Q₀ → S.X₂ → S.X₃ with S using the epimorphism η and identity middle and last maps. Exactness at P₁ follows by comparing Q₁ → Q₀ → S.X₁ with Q₁ → Q₀ → S.X₂ using the monomorphism S.f and identity first and middle maps. Both comparisons use Mathlib ShortComplex.exact_iff_of_epi_of_isIso_of_mono. Higher degrees inherit Q.exact_succ. The augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism by ChainComplex.quasiIsoAt₀_iff and quasiIsoAt_iff_exactAt'. Thus P is a projective resolution of S.X₃.

For either fixed resolution form the functor N ↦ resolution ⊗ N, with maps induced by tensoringRight.map g. Mathlib ProjectiveResolution.isoLeftDerivedObj computes Tor from this functor; ProjectiveResolution.leftDerived_app_eq proves that these comparison isomorphisms are natural in N [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules]. This is the private helper torResolutionIso.

Write i = n+1. The three terms of P ⊗ N in degrees n+3,n+2,n+1 coincide with the terms of Q ⊗ N in degrees n+2,n+1,n, including both differentials and the maps induced by g. Identity components therefore give a natural isomorphism of short-complex functors (spliceScIso). Apply ShortComplex.homologyFunctor and HomologicalComplex.homologyFunctorIso' to obtain spliceHomologyIso in degrees n+2 and n+1. Compose with torResolutionIso for P and the inverse comparison for Q. The components give θ; naturality of this composite gives precisely the required equation.

lean.statement: theorem tor_dimension_shift_natural {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (S : ShortComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R)) (hS : S.ShortExact) [Module.Free R S.X₂] (i : ℕ) (hi : 1 ≤ i) : ∃ θ : ∀ N : ModuleCat.{u} R, (((Tor' (ModuleCat.{u} R) (i + 1)).obj S.X₃).obj N) ≅ (((Tor' (ModuleCat.{u} R) i).obj S.X₁).obj N), ∀ (N N' : ModuleCat.{u} R) (g : N ⟶ N'), ((Tor' (ModuleCat.{u} R) (i + 1)).obj S.X₃).map g ≫ (θ N').hom = (θ N).hom ≫ ((Tor' (ModuleCat.{u} R) i).obj S.X₁).map g

reviewed_lean.note: comm ring R (Type u); 0->K->F->M->0 as S : ShortComplex (ModuleCat R) + S.ShortExact (mono/epi/exact); F free = Module.Free R S.X2; i>=1 as hi : 1<=i; theta_N : Tor'_{i+1}(S.X3,N) iso Tor'_i(S.X1,N) for all N (Tor' resolves first variable, as M1); naturality Tor_{i+1}(M,g) >> theta N' = theta N >> Tor_i(K,g) for all g : N -> N', matches node order
